preamble: Spirantization of a uvular stop to a velar fricative. In Georgian the Old Georgian uvular stop written ჴ (qar), described as /q/ or /qʰ/, merged with the velar fricative ხ /x/ and the letter fell out of use (ჴელი qeli > ხელი xeli 'hand', ჴმაჲ qmay > ხმა xma 'voice'). In Azerbaijani the Turkic back-vowel stop [q] became [x] in syllable codas: Old Anatolian Turkish çoq gave çox 'much', and words still spelled with q are pronounced with [x] finally (ayaq [ɑˈjɑx] 'foot'), while in onsets the same sound became /g/. Spirantizations that end in a uvular fricative, such as Chuvash хура 'black' and Mongolian хар [χar], belong to the q > χ cell.

examples.note: Old Georgian uvular ჴ merged with velar ხ /x/ (phonetically ranging from velar to uvular depending on context). The atlas has no separate aspirated-uvular symbol, so the change is filed under q.

examples.to: Modern Georgian ხმა xma 'voice, sound; vote'
examples.note: Inherited from Proto-Georgian-Zan *qam-, *qm-; Old Georgian ჴ is replaced by ხ in the modern spelling.

examples.from: Old Anatolian Turkish çoq 'much, many' (Proto-Turkic *čok, Turkish çok)
examples.note: Coda q became the velar fricative, now written x.
Orthographic q is /g/ but is spirantized to [x] in codas; this [x] stays velar, while lexical /x/ is often uvular [χ] in colloquial speech.
